1.question: The authority to search Vehicles, Other Carriers under Section 222 of CMTA extends to persons, animals when they are suspected of:

choices.A: Holding and Conveying illegal goods
choices.B: Carrying personal belongings without declaration
choices.C: Holding or conveying dutiable or prohibited goods
choices.D: Holding or conveying dutiable or forfeitable goods

1.reason: Section 222 of the CMTA provides that the authority to stop, search, and examine extends to vehicles, carriers, persons, or animals suspected of holding or conveying dutiable or prohibited goods.

2.question: Who submits an adequate statement of the facts involved in rulings if the matter is not otherwise appealed for review in ordinary course?

choices.A: Deputy Commissioner
choices.B: District Collector
choices.C: Commissioner
choices.D: Customs Officer

2.reason: Under the CMTA framework, the District Collector submits an adequate statement of the facts involved in rulings when the matter is not otherwise appealed for review in the ordinary course.

3.question: The Commissioner may delegate powers vested upon him under CMTA and this can be delegated to any customs officers with rank of division chief or higher. What may be delegated by the Commissioner?

choices.A: Issuance of a Notice of Seizure
choices.B: Issuance of an Alert Order
choices.C: Issuance of a Mission Order
choices.D: All of the above may not be delegated by the Commissioner

3.reason: Under Section 201(e) of the CMTA, the Commissioner may delegate powers to any customs officer with the rank equivalent to division chief or higher. The non-delegable powers are: (1) promulgation of rules and regulations; (2) issuance, revocation or modification of rulings; and (3) compromise or abatement of customs obligations. Issuance of a Notice of Seizure is not among the non-delegable powers.

choices.B: AMO
choices.C: RMO
choices.D: Office of the District Collector

5.question: Under CMTA, when should the special surveillance of vessels/aircrafts and cargoes on board start?

choices.B: Upon completion of boarding formalities.

choices.D: Upon Entry into Philippine Territory.

6.question: A Deputation Order was issued by Collector of Customs to Police Captain Mark Balolong for his exercise of police authority. Is this a valid Deputation Order?

choices.A: Yes, because the authority shall be exercised outside of customs premises.

choices.C: No, because the exercise of police authority is subject to approval of the Secretary of Finance.
choices.D: No, because the authority is not valid under CMTA.

6.reason: A Deputation Order must be issued by the Commissioner of Customs, not by a Collector of Customs. The authority to deputize law enforcement agencies is vested in the Commissioner under CMTA.

7.question: What is the immediate significance of a vessel loaded with imported goods enter the Philippine territory to discharge laden goods?

choices.A: Duties and taxes will be collected on the imported goods.
choices.B: Importation begins.
choices.C: Vessel will undergo boarding formalities.

7.reason: Importation begins when a vessel carrying imported goods enters the Philippine territory with the intention to discharge laden goods. This triggers customs jurisdiction over the goods.

8.question: Is there a need for a Mission Order (MO) to implement a Letter of Authority (LOA)?

choices.A: A LOA may be implemented without a need for a Mission Order.
choices.B: A Mission Order must be issued to authorize the implementation of a LOA.
choices.C: If LOA is exercised within customs premises, there is no need for a MO.
choices.D: It depends on the Commissioner of Customs.

13.question: When is importation deemed terminated if the imported goods are subject to payment of customs duties and taxes?

choices.A: Upon lodgement of goods declaration

choices.C: Upon payment of customs duties and taxes and legal permit for withdrawal has been granted.
choices.D: Upon delivery to the consignee's place.

13.reason: Under Papa v. Mago, importation is terminated only upon the payment of duties, taxes and other charges upon the articles, or secured to be paid, at the port of entry and the legal permit for withdrawal shall have been granted.

14.question: What is the prescribed time frame for a beneficiary of an Advance Ruling on Valuation to file for extension of period of the validity of the Advance Ruling?

choices.A: Application for revalidation must be filed at any time before expiration of the Advance Ruling
choices.B: Must be filed at least 60 days before expiration

choices.D: Must be filed at least 90 calendar days before expiration

15.question: How shall the Philippines be divided for administrative purposes and efficient discharge of the functions of the Bureau of Customs bureaucracy?

choices.D: The Philippines shall be divided into as many Ports of Entry as necessary.

16.question: Is the Collector of Mariveles correct on his contention?

choices.A: President of the BOC

18.question: Which of the following may not be delegated by the Commissioner of Customs to a subordinate customs officer?

choices.A: Compromise or abatement of customs obligations.
choices.B: Issuance, revocation or modification of rulings.
choices.C: Prohibition of rules and regulations.
choices.D: All of the above cannot be delegated by the Commissioner.

19.question: A Customs Personnel Order (CPO) signed by the Commissioner and the Secretary of Finance designating the Deputy Commissioner, AOCG as the full authority to accept applications for Advance Ruling on Valuation, process and approve the same. Is this a valid delegation of power vested upon the Commissioner under CMTA?

21.question: Locator "A" operating in Subic Freeport Zone would like to sell a portion of its production out to a company operating in the customs territory. choices.C: Transaction value of the imported raw materials.

22.question: The officials of the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) conducted a search for the purpose of checking proper handling and packaging of imported wines and cigarettes imported by Asthe Inc. 29.question: A Bureau official proposes automating the enforcement of customs laws, including jurisdiction over forfeiture cases. How should the Bureau approach this proposal?

choices.D: The Bureau can approve the automation system, but retain exclusive original jurisdiction over forfeiture cases.

31.question: Which case pertains to the Bureau of Customs exclusive jurisdiction over seized and forfeited cars and RTC are devoid of any competence to pass upon the validity or regularity of seizure and forfeiture proceedings conducted by the BOC?

choices.B: Papa v. Mago G.R. No. L-27360 22, SCRA 857
choices.C: Remigio v. Sandiganbayan, 374 SCRA 114

32.question: Which case pertains to the issue on the ordered release of 25,000 sacks of imported rice to the claimants, not withstanding the pendency of seizure and forfeiture proceedings before the Bureau of Customs?

choices.B: Emile v. Vinuya
choices.C: Papa v. Mago
choices.D: Rallos v. Gako Jr.

choices.D: Tariff Commission

choices.A: District Collector for the port that he has jurisdiction.

36.question: An application for an Advance Ruling on origin from a construction company was submitted to BOC for a special design roof, steel window and modular concrete wall to be imported from Malaysia. How shall BOC handle the application?

choices.A: BOC shall request for total amount of P4,500 as application fee.

37.question: An application for an Advance Ruling on ROO from a construction company was submitted to BOC for a special design roof, steel window and modular concrete wall to be imported from Malaysia. How shall BOC handle the application?

choices.D: BOC shall deny the application and refund the application fee paid.

38.question: What is the CMTA provision with regard to the time frame by which an applicant to an Advance Ruling shall be notified by the Bureau of Customs on the fact that an Advance Ruling has been issued?

choices.A: The notification must be done electronically within 3 working days from issuance of the Advance Ruling.

choices.A: June 5, 2025

choices.D: July 4, 2025

42.question: An applicant believes that the Advance Ruling issued by the Commissioner is not correct. How will he protect his interest?

43.question: The Commissioner of Customs invalidate an issued Advance Ruling and as a result a motion for reconsideration was filed. If the Commissioner denies the motion for reconsideration what is the appeal remedy for the aggrieved party?

choices.A: Appeal to the Secretary of Finance within 30 days.

46.question: What is an exception to the 15-day appeal period to the Commissioner of a decision of a District Collector?

choices.A: All appeals to the Commissioner of a decision of a District Collector is 15 days.
choices.B: Appeal in the case of compulsory acquisition.

47.question: May an appeal be filed even without any supporting documents?

choices.A: No, because Commissioner would not have any basis to render a decision.

50.question: As of now not all CMTA provisions have been covered by implementing rules and regulations. 51.question: Matters considered as confidential may be released upon request of general public?

choices.A: Upon the discretion of the Commissioner of Customs

53.question: An importation purportedly duty and tax exempt was released from customs custody without the covering Tax Exempt Indorsement issued by DOF as provided for by regulation. choices.A: Yes, as the law provides that in case of duty and tax exempt goods its importation is deemed terminated once it has legally left the jurisdiction of the Bureau of Customs.
choices.B: No

258.question: To secure a search warrant for a dwelling, what specific facts must be detailed in the sworn application?

choices.A: The sworn application must show probable cause and particularly describe the person who is going to conduct the search.
choices.B: The sworn application must show probable cause and particularly describe the place to be searched and goods to be seized.
choices.C: The sworn application must show probable cause and particularly describe the place to be searched, the owner of the place, and the value of the goods to be seized.
choices.D: The sworn application must show probable cause and particularly describe the place to be searched, and the value of the goods to be seized.

258.reason: The sworn application must show probable cause and particularly describe the place to be searched and the goods to be seized.

259.question: When an actual seizure transpires due to the failure of the importer or possessor to provide proof of tax payment, where will the funding for the incurred expenses be sourced?

choices.A: Intelligence Fund of the Commissioner of Customs.
choices.B: Intelligence Fund of the District Collector.
choices.C: Forfeiture Fund.
choices.D: It depends on the availability of cash from any of the choices.

259.reason: Expenses incurred during seizure are sourced from the Forfeiture Fund.

260.question: Which Supreme Court decision establishes that criminal prosecution related to customs violations under the Tariff and Customs Code is no longer viable under the new CMTA?

choices.A: Calvo v. UCPB General Insurance Co., Inc G.R. No. 149496, March 19, 2002 379 SCRA 510
choices.B: Remigio v. Sandiganbayan, January 18, 2002 374 SCRA 114
choices.C: Kasparan ng mga Nagsisitinda sa Pamantasan ng Pilipinas v. Tan G.R. No. 81311, June 30 1988
choices.D: De Guzman v. Court of Appeals in relation to Article 1732 Civil Code of the Philippines.

260.reason: Remigio v. Sandiganbayan established that criminal prosecution under the old Tariff and Customs Code is no longer viable under the CMTA.

261.question: Under CMTA Section 222, who is permitted to apply for a judicial search warrant specifically for entering a dwelling house?

choices.A: The Commissioner and his Deputy Commissioner may apply for a judicial search warrant.
choices.B: Only officers in the Legal Service may apply for a judicial search warrant.
choices.C: Only the Commissioner and his Deputy Commissioner may apply for a judicial search warrant.
choices.D: Any of the choices.

261.reason: Under Section 222 of the CMTA, only the Commissioner and his Deputy Commissioner may apply for a judicial search warrant to enter a dwelling house.

262.question: Which specific official is authorized to petition for a judicial search warrant targeting a dwelling house under Section 222 of the CMTA?

choices.A: The Commissioner and his Deputy Commissioner may apply for a judicial search warrant.
choices.B: Only officers in the Legal Service may apply for a judicial search warrant.
choices.C: Only the Commissioner and his Deputy Commissioner may apply for a judicial search warrant.
choices.D: Any of the choices.

262.reason: Only the Commissioner and his Deputy Commissioner may apply for a judicial search warrant for a dwelling house under Section 222.

263.question: Is it a conclusive rule that the Bureau of Customs exercises absolute control over customs premises and facilities?

choices.A: Yes, because tax is the lifeblood of the economy.
choices.B: No, because such power is without prejudice to the general police power of the local government units, the PCG, and law enforcement agencies in the exercise of their functions.
choices.C: Yes, because the control of customs jurisdiction does not admit any exception.
choices.D: Any of the above depending on the situation.

263.reason: The Bureau's control over customs premises is not absolute; it is without prejudice to the functions of LGUs, PCG, and other law enforcement agencies.

264.question: Which parties are mandated by the CMTA to facilitate unrestricted access to their premises for customs officers exercising police powers?

choices.A: District Collectors.
choices.B: Deputy District Collectors.
choices.C: Port and airport authorities in all ports of entry.
choices.D: All of the above.

264.reason: Port and airport authorities are mandated to facilitate unrestricted access to their premises for customs officers.

265.question: The BIR conducted a search to verify taxes on imported goods. Is the search lawful if the authorization letter was exclusively signed by the District Collector?

choices.A: No, as per Section 214 of CMTA.
choices.B: No, because the letter must be signed by the Commissioner of Customs.
choices.C: Yes, because LOA may be signed by the Commissioner of Customs.
choices.D: Yes, because CMTA is not applicable in this case.

265.reason: Under CMTA, the Letter of Authority must be signed by the Commissioner of Customs, not merely by the District Collector.

266.question: Which official is granted the authority to assign or reassign customs officers?

choices.A: Commissioner of Customs
choices.B: District Collector subject to approval of the Commissioner of Customs.
choices.C: Commissioner of Customs subject to approval of the Secretary of Finance.
choices.D: Secretary of Finance subject to approval of the President of the Philippines.

266.reason: Under Section 201(f), the Commissioner of Customs may assign or reassign customs officers subject to the approval of the Secretary of Finance.

267.question: During an inspection where the importer fails to produce payment documentation, an inventory of the goods is conducted. What is the procedure for utilizing the prepared Inventory Report?

choices.A: Present to the District Collector for purposes of issuance of Warrant of Seizure and Detention (WSD).
choices.B: Furnish copy of the Inventory Report to the concerned customs officers who will place the place of visit on 24/7 underguarding.
choices.C: Furnish copy of the Inventory Report to the concerned Law Division for forfeiture proceedings purposes.
choices.D: Furnish copy of the Inventory Report to the owner, occupant or person in possession of the goods, receipt of which must be properly acknowledged.

267.reason: A copy of the Inventory Report must be furnished to the owner, occupant, or person in possession of the goods, with proper acknowledgment of receipt.

268.question: Which official is vested with the authority to promulgate the implementing rules for the establishment of temporary warehousing facilities for imported goods, pending declaration, in instances of abandonment or overstaying cargo?

choices.A: District Collector for the port that he has jurisdiction.
choices.B: President of the Philippines.
choices.C: Secretary of Finance.
choices.D: Commissioner of Customs.

268.reason: The Commissioner of Customs has the authority to issue rules for the establishment of temporary warehousing facilities for imported goods.

269.question: If, during an inspection, the importer fails to provide proof of payment within the legal timeframe, how should the Bureau of Customs proceed?

choices.A: Imported goods may be forfeited in favor of the government.
choices.B: Surcharge of 25% shall be imposed.
choices.C: Imported goods may be seized and subjected to forfeiture proceedings.
choices.D: Any of the choices is valid.

269.reason: If proof of payment is not provided, the goods may be seized and subjected to forfeiture proceedings.

270.question: Who possesses the supervisory control and oversight over any designated Deputy District Collector?

choices.A: District Collector for his jurisdiction and the Deputy District Collector is assigned to sub-ports.
choices.B: District Collector for the designated District Collector.
choices.C: Any Deputy Customs Appraiser designated at the District Collector.
choices.D: Any of the choices.

270.reason: The District Collector exercises supervisory control over Deputy District Collectors assigned to sub-ports within his jurisdiction.

271.question: Which specific jurisprudence affirms that the Bureau of Customs holds exclusive jurisdiction over forfeiture proceedings, rendering the RTC devoid of jurisdiction to intervene?

choices.A: Emile v. Vinuya G.R. No. L-29043 37 SCRA 381
choices.B: Papa v. Mago G.R. No. L-27360 22, SCRA 857
choices.C: Remigio v. Sandiganbayan, 374 SCRA 114
choices.D: Asian Terminals Inc., v. Bautista Ricafort, 505 SCRA 748

271.reason: Emile v. Vinuya affirmed the BOC's exclusive jurisdiction over forfeiture proceedings, preventing RTC intervention.

272.question: Who bears the legal accountability for ensuring the proper entry of all imported goods into the customs office?

choices.A: District Collector.
choices.B: Commissioner of Customs.
choices.C: Deputy Commissioner, Enforcement Group.
choices.D: All of the above.

272.reason: The District Collector bears accountability for ensuring the proper entry of all imported goods into the customs office.

273.question: Who is granted the authority to designate non-customs infrastructure such as public wharves, landing areas, or streets for customs-related objectives?

choices.A: President subject to approval of Secretary of Finance
choices.B: Commissioner of Customs
choices.C: Commissioner of Customs subject to approval of the Secretary of Finance.
choices.D: President of the Philippines

273.reason: The Commissioner of Customs may designate non-customs infrastructure for customs purposes, subject to the approval of the Secretary of Finance.

274.question: If, during an inventory inspection of foreign merchandise, restricted or regulated items are discovered, and the possessor cannot present valid regulatory permits or licenses, what course of action must the visiting customs officials take?

choices.A: The goods shall be seized.
choices.B: The visiting customs officers shall recommend to the Commissioner of Customs the issuance of WSD.
choices.C: The visiting customs officers are authorized to immediately condemn the goods.
choices.D: The visiting customs officers must immediately refer the matter to the concerned regulatory agency or agencies.

274.reason: When restricted or regulated goods are discovered without permits, the matter must be referred to the concerned regulatory agency.

275.question: This term represents the procedure used by Customs to ensure accuracy by examining the relevant business records, books, and commercial systems. What is this procedure called?

choices.A: Audit Based Control
choices.B: Customs Control
choices.C: Customs Clearance
choices.D: Audit Examination

275.reason: Audit Based Control is the procedure of examining business records, books, and commercial systems to ensure accuracy.

276.question: Police Captain Peter de la Cruz was issued a Deputation Order to conduct visits and inspections. Does this issuance constitute a valid Deputation Order under customs law?

choices.A: Yes, because the authority shall be exercised outside of customs premises.
choices.B: No, because the exercise of power to visit and inspect is exclusive to customs officers.
choices.C: No, because the exercise of power to visit and inspect is subject to approval of the Secretary of Finance.
choices.D: Yes, because the power to visit and inspect is in the exercise of police authority under CMTA.

276.reason: The power to visit and inspect is exclusive to customs officers and cannot be delegated to police officers through a Deputation Order.

277.question: Which group of persons is explicitly barred from exercising police authority under the provisions of the CMTA?

choices.A: Customs Inspectors
choices.B: Customs Appraisers
choices.C: Warehouse Guards
choices.D: All of the above are authorized to perform police authority.

277.reason: Customs Inspectors, Customs Appraisers, and Warehouse Guards are all authorized to exercise police authority under the CMTA.

278.question: During an inspection, what is the prescribed time limit within which the importer must present proof of payment?

choices.A: Within thirty (30) days from demand
choices.B: Within fifteen (15) days from demand
choices.C: Within thirty (30) days from demand
choices.D: Within forty-eight (48) hours from demand

278.reason: The importer must present proof of payment within fifteen (15) days from demand.

279.question: Is the PNP, AFP, or other law enforcement agencies legally compelled to render assistance for search, seizure, or arrest during the exercise of CMTA-granted police authority?

choices.A: No, giving assistance is only on voluntary basis as they may also be busy in the discharge of their official functions.
choices.B: Yes, it is the duty of any police officer and other national law enforcers to give such lawful assistance.
choices.C: No, as the mandate of these law enforcement agencies does not involve customs work.
choices.D: Any of the choices.

279.reason: It is the duty of police officers and other national law enforcers to render lawful assistance in customs operations.

280.question: An NBI team conducted a search based on a Letter of Authority signed by their Commissioner, along with a letter from the District Collector. Is this search considered legally valid?

choices.A: Yes, because the LOA is valid.
choices.B: Yes, because the seizure is valid.
choices.C: No, the search is not valid because it was signed by the District Collector.
choices.D: No, the seizure is not valid. Under Sec 214.

280.reason: The search is not valid because the Letter of Authority must be signed by the Commissioner of Customs, not the District Collector.

281.question: What categories of goods define the actual scope, nature, or extent of a lawful customs search?

choices.A: Prohibited goods
choices.B: Prohibited and confiscated goods
choices.C: Licit goods
choices.D: All of the above

281.reason: A lawful customs search may cover prohibited goods, confiscated goods, and even licit goods when there is reasonable suspicion.

282.question: A deputized national law enforcement officer is required to maintain ongoing coordination with which specific customs official?

choices.A: Deputy Commissioner, Enforcement Group
choices.B: Commissioner of Customs
choices.C: Deputy Commissioner, Intelligence Group
choices.D: All of the above

282.reason: Deputized officers must maintain coordination with the Commissioner of Customs.

283.question: Over which of the following areas may the power to inspect and visit be properly exercised?

choices.A: Customs bonded warehouses.
choices.B: On places where imported goods are sold openly or kept in storage.
choices.C: On carrying vessel or aircraft.
choices.D: All of the above.

283.reason: The power to inspect and visit may be exercised over customs bonded warehouses, places where imported goods are kept or sold, and on vessels or aircraft.

284.question: If no Deputy District Collector is available to fill in for an absent District Collector, who makes the designation?

choices.A: It shall be the Commissioner of Customs who shall make the designation.
choices.B: It shall be the Commissioner of Customs subject to approval of the Secretary of Finance.
choices.C: The District Collector would have to wait for an available Deputy District Collector that he may designate.
choices.D: District Collector shall designate in writing a senior ranking customs officer to temporarily perform his duties.

284.reason: The District Collector shall designate in writing a senior ranking customs officer to temporarily perform his duties.

285.question: How many Deputy District Collectors are permitted to assist the District Collector?

choices.A: For seaports: Three (3) Deputy District Collector for Assessment, Deputy District Collector for Operations, Deputy District Collector for Administration.
choices.B: For airports: Four (4) – Deputy District Collector for Assessment, Deputy District Collector for Passenger Service, Deputy District Collector for Administration and Deputy District Collector for Operations.
choices.C: As many as may be necessary.
choices.D: All of the above.

285.reason: The number of Deputy District Collectors varies depending on the port type; seaports have 3 while airports have 4, and as many as necessary.

286.question: The Commissioner, with the Finance Secretary's approval, can reassign customs personnel. What are the constraints on this re-assignment power?

choices.A: Such assignment shall not affect the employee's tenure of office.
choices.B: Such assignment shall not result in the change of status of the employee.
choices.C: Such assignment shall not result in demotion in rank and/or salary deduction.
choices.D: All of the Above.

286.reason: Reassignment shall not affect tenure, change status, or result in demotion or salary deduction.

287.question: At which specific type of port is the District Collector officially designated to hold office?

choices.A: Port of entry.
choices.B: Principal port of entry.
choices.C: Sub-port of entry.
choices.D: It depends on the business situation of the port.

287.reason: The District Collector is officially designated at the principal port of entry.

288.question: Which customs officials may be delegated the authority by the Commissioner to exercise inspection and visitation functions?

choices.A: Deputy Commissioner, Intelligence Group
choices.B: Deputy Commissioner, Enforcement Group
choices.C: Customs officers
choices.D: All of the above

288.reason: The Commissioner may delegate inspection and visitation functions to customs officers.

289.question: When exercising police authority, officials may force entry by opening gates. Whose physical presence is mandated for such an action to be permissible?

choices.A: Presence of the owner of the imported goods.
choices.B: Presence of the owner of the place to be entered.
choices.C: Presence of either the District Collector who has territorial jurisdiction over the place or his authorized representative.
choices.D: Presence of Punong Barangay or his authorized representative and the police having jurisdiction over the area.

289.reason: The District Collector or his authorized representative must be present when forcing entry by opening gates.

290.question: What essential details are required to be stated within a Mission Order?

choices.A: The specific names of the persons involved in the mission.
choices.B: The duration of the mission and the budget allocated.
choices.C: The office where the mission originates and the place of assignment.
choices.D: The rank of the personnel involved and the place of assignment.

290.reason: The Mission Order must state the specific names of the persons involved in the mission.

291.question: How frequently is the District Collector required to report on all district-level transactions to the Commissioner?

choices.A: Monthly.
choices.B: Bi-monthly.
choices.C: Quarterly.
choices.D: Semi-annual.

291.reason: The District Collector is required to report monthly on all district-level transactions to the Commissioner.

292.question: When customs officials, in the course of serving a Letter of Authority (LOA), uncover prohibited articles, what is the mandatory procedure?

choices.A: The prohibited goods shall be condemned.
choices.B: The matter shall be referred to the concerned regulatory agency.
choices.C: The prohibited goods shall be subject to constructive seizure.
choices.D: The prohibited goods shall be confiscated.

292.reason: When prohibited articles are uncovered during LOA service, the matter shall be referred to the concerned regulatory agency.

293.question: What essential information must be included in a sworn application for a search warrant to legally enter and search a private residence?

choices.A: The sworn application must show probable cause and particularly describe the person who is going to conduct search.
choices.B: The sworn application must show probable cause and particularly describe the person who is going to conduct search.
choices.C: The sworn application must show probable cause and particularly describe the place to be searched and goods to be seized.
choices.D: The sworn application must show probable cause and particularly describe the place to be searched, the owner of the place, and the value of the goods to be seized.

293.reason: The sworn application must show probable cause and particularly describe the place to be searched and the goods to be seized.

294.question: Which joint memorandum order executed by the heads of the BIR, BOC, and DOF is relevant to this specific customs matter?

choices.A: Joint memorandum order signed by the heads of BIR, BOC and DOF.
choices.B: Commissioner of Customs subject to approval of the Secretary of Finance.
choices.C: Joint memorandum order signed by the heads of BIR, BOC and DOF.
choices.D: Any of the choices.

294.reason: The Joint Memorandum Order signed by the heads of BIR, BOC, and DOF governs customs matters involving tax verification.

295.question: Who is vested with the right to legally change the official name of a Customs District?

choices.A: President of the Philippines.
choices.B: Secretary of Finance subject to approval of the President of the Philippines.
choices.C: Commissioner of Customs subject to approval of the Secretary of Finance.
choices.D: Commissioner of Customs.

295.reason: The Commissioner of Customs may change the name of a Customs District, subject to the approval of the Secretary of Finance.

296.question: When searching vessels, customs may remove false compartments. Under what situations might the officer be held responsible for resulting damages?

choices.A: The search was done when vessel has not entered the Collection District which is the port of discharge.
choices.B: The search was done before boarding formalities.
choices.C: There is gross negligence or abuse of authority in the exercise of the authority.
choices.D: All of the above.

296.reason: An officer may be held liable for damages only when there is gross negligence or abuse of authority in exercising search powers.

297.question: To whom should a deputized official immediately surrender custody of seized goods?

choices.A: Seized goods shall be turned over to any customs officer to handle.
choices.B: Seized goods shall be turned over to a qualified customs officer.
choices.C: Seized goods shall be turned over to a qualified customs officer.
choices.D: Any of the choices.

297.reason: Seized goods shall be turned over to a qualified customs officer for proper custody.

298.question: Does a hot pursuit of a customs violator in international waters constitute a valid exercise of customs jurisdiction?

choices.A: No, because this would be a violation of international law.
choices.B: Yes, because but seizure may only be effected in the high seas or international air space.
choices.C: Yes, because customs is not bound by territorial boundaries.
choices.D: None of the choices.

298.reason: Hot pursuit into international waters is a valid exercise of customs jurisdiction, and seizure may be effected in the high seas.

299.question: The authority to search under CMTA extends to persons or animals based on which suspicion?

choices.A: Holding and conveying illegal goods.
choices.B: Carrying personal belongings without declaration.
choices.C: Holding or conveying dutiable or prohibited goods.
choices.D: Holding or conveying dutiable or forfeitable goods.

299.reason: The authority to search extends to persons or animals suspected of holding or conveying dutiable or prohibited goods under Section 222.

300.question: How should the Commissioner properly delegate the authority to an individual for the purpose of inspection and visitation?

choices.A: Verbal instructions may suffice.
choices.B: Verbal instructions and written order to follow may suffice.
choices.C: It may be exercised through any Deputy Commissioner of Customs.
choices.D: It must be in writing.

300.reason: The delegation of authority for inspection and visitation must be in writing.

301.question: Who is given the legal authority to reassign customs staff upon the closure of a specific port of entry?

choices.A: District Collector subject to approval of the Commissioner of Customs.
choices.B: District Collector.
choices.C: Commissioner of Customs.
choices.D: Commissioner of Customs subject to approval of the Secretary of Finance.

301.reason: The Commissioner of Customs may reassign customs staff upon port closure, subject to the approval of the Secretary of Finance.

302.question: Does the CMTA mandate the PNP and AFP to assist in customs searches and seizures?

choices.A: No, giving assistance is only on voluntary basis as they may also be busy in the discharge of their official functions.
choices.B: Yes, it is the duty of any police officer and other national law enforcers to give such lawful assistance.
choices.C: No, as the mandate of these law enforcement agencies does not involve customs work.
choices.D: Any of the choices.

302.reason: It is the duty of police officers and other national law enforcers to render lawful assistance in customs operations.

303.question: Which CMTA section addresses the legal implications of 'Trespass or Obstruction of Customs Premises'?

choices.A: Sec. 304
choices.B: Sec. 303
choices.C: Sec. 306
choices.D: Sec. 305

303.reason: Section 303 of the CMTA addresses Trespass or Obstruction of Customs Premises.

304.question: What is the proper charge to the Bureau of Customs for the suitable areas and equipment provided by port operators?

choices.A: Reasonable amount.
choices.B: Below the commercial rates as approved by the concerned port or airport authorities.
choices.C: It should be free of charge.
choices.D: Any of the choices.

304.reason: Port operators should provide suitable areas and equipment free of charge to the Bureau of Customs.

305.question: When is a person exercising customs police authority allowed to enter and search non-residential structures?

choices.A: Office hours only.
choices.B: After office hours only if entry during office hours not possible.
choices.C: At any time of the day.
choices.D: It depends on the person in charge of places to be entered.

305.reason: Customs police authority may enter and search non-residential structures at any time of the day.

306.question: If two senior customs officers are available to replace an absent District Collector, how is the duration of their temporary duties split?

choices.A: The period is a matter of agreement between the two (2) senior ranking officers.
choices.B: The period is a matter of agreement between the two (2) senior ranking officers.
choices.C: It depends on the sound discretion of the District Collector as to what will apportion the period by which the District Collector is to discharge the duties.
choices.D: By the number of days.

306.reason: The period is a matter of agreement between the two senior ranking officers.

307.question: What designated officials are permitted by the Commissioner to execute the power of inspection and visitation?

choices.A: Deputy Commissioner, Enforcement Group
choices.B: Deputy Commissioner, Intelligence Group
choices.C: Customs officers
choices.D: All of the above

307.reason: The Commissioner may permit customs officers to execute the power of inspection and visitation.

308.question: All goods entering or exiting customs territory are subject to customs control. Are the carrier vessels and aircraft also subject to this control?

choices.A: No, because such vessels and aircraft are not the subject of importation or exportation.
choices.B: No, because the jurisdiction and control is with the Maritime Industry Authority or Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines as the case may be.
choices.C: Yes, as provided for under CMTA.
choices.D: Yes, as they may also be subject to payment of customs duties and taxes.

308.reason: Carrier vessels and aircraft are also subject to customs control as provided under CMTA.

309.question: If a customs officer is asked about their authority while acting, what constitutes their appropriate course of action?

choices.A: The authorized person shall present his credentials and warrant of seizure.
choices.B: The authorized person shall disclose the source of information on why search is being conducted.
choices.C: The authorized person shall disclose the nature of the authority and exhibit the corresponding written authority issued by the Commissioner of Customs.
choices.D: Any of the above.

309.reason: The customs officer shall disclose the nature of the authority and exhibit the corresponding written authority issued by the Commissioner.

310.question: Who has the power to declare privately-owned infrastructure like wharves or landing places as customs-designated areas?

choices.A: District Collector who has territorial jurisdiction over the port.
choices.B: Commissioner of Customs.
choices.C: Commissioner of Customs subject to approval of the Secretary of Finance.
choices.D: President of the Philippines.

310.reason: The Commissioner of Customs may declare privately-owned infrastructure as customs-designated areas, subject to SOF approval.

311.question: Can a Mission Order be rescinded prior to its full implementation or execution?

choices.A: It may only be revoked during its period of validity.
choices.B: Only the completion of the mission may cause the revocation of the Mission Order.
choices.C: Yes, if the mission becomes legally impossible to achieve.
choices.D: None of the choices.

311.reason: A Mission Order may be rescinded if the mission becomes legally impossible to achieve.

312.question: Under what conditions or grounds can an alert order be legally maintained?

choices.A: Prevention of unlawful importation, exportation of articles or goods.
choices.B: Intelligence report on smuggling activities of specific persons or firms.
choices.C: Intelligence report on smuggling activities as provided under CMTA.
choices.D: All of the above.

312.reason: Alert orders may be maintained on any of the stated grounds including prevention of unlawful importation/exportation or intelligence reports on smuggling.

313.question: Who possesses the authority to officially issue a Deputation Order?

choices.A: Only the Commissioner of Customs may issue a Deputation Order.
choices.B: The Commissioner of Customs and any customs officer he authorizes in writing may issue a Deputation Order.
choices.C: Aside from the Commissioner of Customs, District Collectors within his territorial jurisdiction may issue a Deputation Order.
choices.D: The Commissioner of Customs has exclusive authority to issue a Deputation Order subject to approval of the Customs Personnel Order (CPO) by the Secretary of Finance.

313.reason: Only the Commissioner of Customs may issue a Deputation Order.

314.question: What is the designated Collection District for the sub-port of Jordan?

choices.A: Tacloban
choices.B: Cebu
choices.C: Iloilo
choices.D: Batangas

314.reason: The sub-port of Jordan is under Collection District No. VI - Iloilo.

315.question: Which official is vested with the authority to promulgate the implementing rules for the establishment of temporary warehousing facilities for imported goods, pending declaration, in instances of abandonment or overstaying cargo?

choices.A: District Collector for the port that he has jurisdiction.
choices.B: President of the Philippines.
choices.C: Secretary of Finance.
choices.D: Commissioner of Customs.

315.reason: The Commissioner of Customs has the authority to issue rules for the establishment of temporary warehousing facilities for imported goods.

316.question: Which document shall comprehensively describe the procedures, scope, and guidelines governing police authority and the custody of seized items?

choices.A: Joint Memorandum Order among the Bureau of Customs, Department of Finance, AFP, and PNP.
choices.B: Commissioner of Customs subject to approval of the Secretary of Finance.
choices.C: Joint Memorandum Order among BIR, BOC and DOF.
choices.D: Any of the choices.

316.reason: The Joint Memorandum Order among BOC, DOF, AFP, and PNP describes the procedures for police authority and custody of seized items.

317.question: During forfeiture proceedings, if payment proof is suddenly presented, what is the immediate proper action for the District Collector?

choices.A: District Collector must immediately terminate the proceedings and issue an order of release.
choices.B: District Collector shall cause the immediate release of the goods within fifteen (15) days from receipt of motion to quash warrant of seizure after finding that the evidence presented are authentic and in order subject to clearance by the Commissioner.
choices.C: The District Collector must check if the evidence presented are in order and authentic and forward the case to the Commissioner of Customs for appropriate action.
choices.D: The District Collector must check the authenticity and if the evidence presented are in order and imposed 10% surcharge. Then the matter shall be referred to the Commissioner for proper action.

317.reason: The District Collector must check if the evidence is authentic and in order, then forward the case to the Commissioner for appropriate action.

318.question: Do you concur with the proposition that Collection Districts must operate under uniform staffing levels and working times?

choices.A: Yes, for consistency purposes
choices.B: No, as the business needs or requirements of each Collection District varies.
choices.C: Yes, pursuant to Civil Service Commission (CSC) rules and regulations.
choices.D: No, as the salaries in the primary Collection Districts located in first class cities should be higher.

318.reason: Collection Districts need not have uniform staffing levels as the business requirements vary per district.

319.question: In the event of the District Collector's absence, who is authorized to temporarily assume and discharge the Collector's duties?

choices.A: Joint memorandum order signed by the heads of BIR, BOC and DOF.
choices.B: Commissioner of Customs subject to approval of the Secretary of Finance.
choices.C: Joint memorandum order signed by the heads of BIR, BOC and DOF.
choices.D: Any of the choices.

319.reason: The Commissioner of Customs may authorize a temporary replacement for an absent District Collector, subject to SOF approval.

320.question: During the prescribed 15-day window for the importer to submit proof of settlement upon a visiting officer's demand, what legal presumption applies?

choices.A: It shall be presumed that the importation of the goods is contrary to law.
choices.B: It shall be presumed that duties and taxes have not been paid on the goods.
choices.C: It shall be presumed that the goods as under constructive customs custody.
choices.D: All of the above.

320.reason: All three presumptions apply during the 15-day period: importation is contrary to law, duties unpaid, and goods under constructive custody.

321.question: Who holds the requisite authority to direct a terminal or port operator to relocate overstaying cargoes to an inland storage facility?

choices.A: District Collector who has territorial jurisdiction over the port.
choices.B: President subject to approval of the Secretary of Finance.
choices.C: Commissioner of Customs subject to approval of the Secretary of Finance C.
choices.D: President of the Philippines.

321.reason: The President of the Philippines, through an executive order, may direct the relocation of overstaying cargoes.

322.question: Prior to the Bureau of Customs engaging in the pursuit of imported items subject to seizure, what prerequisite condition must be fulfilled?

choices.A: The Bureau of Customs may only pursue imported goods subject to seizure if Warrant of Seizure has been issued against the goods.
choices.B: The Bureau of Customs may only pursue imported goods subject to seizure if customs duties and taxes are not paid.
choices.C: The Bureau of Customs may only pursue imported goods subject to seizure during its transport by land, water and air.
choices.D: Any of the situation is a legal basis to pursue imported goods.

322.reason: The Bureau may pursue imported goods subject to seizure during transport by land, water, or air.

323.question: Is the assertion accurate that Collection Districts must adhere to a uniform staffing pattern and standard working hours?

choices.A: Yes, for consistency purposes
choices.B: No, as the business needs or requirements of each Collection District varies.
choices.C: Yes, pursuant to Civil Service Commission (CSC) rules and regulations.
choices.D: No, as the salaries in the primary Collection Districts located in first class cities should be higher.

323.reason: Collection Districts need not have uniform staffing patterns as business requirements vary per district.

324.question: What is the primary objective of a controlled delivery operation?

choices.A: To facilitate trade
choices.B: To gather evidence to identify the person involved in smuggling-related offenses, preparatory prosecution of the offender.
choices.C: As risk management tool
choices.D: All of the above

324.reason: The primary objective of controlled delivery is to gather evidence to identify persons involved in smuggling offenses for prosecution.

325.question: What is the accurate description regarding the scope of police authority granted to authorized customs officials?

choices.A: The police authority may only be exercised in areas outside of customs premises.
choices.B: The police authority under CMTA may be exercised by deputized police officers.
choices.C: The police authority may only be exercised in areas outside of customs premises.
choices.D: The police authority granted by deputization of NLEA officers and members is the same as that of a customs officer vested with police authority under CMTA.

325.reason: Police authority under CMTA may be exercised by deputized police officers.

326.question: What limitation, if any, exists on the police authority vested in a deputized law enforcement officer?

choices.A: The police authority granted upon deputization of NLEA officers and members is the same as that of a customs officer vested with police authority under CMTA.
choices.B: The limitation is that the police authority granted does not pertain to making an assessment.
choices.C: The police authority shall only be exercised in areas outside of customs premises.
choices.D: None of the choices.

326.reason: The limitation is that the deputized officer's police authority does not include the power to make assessments.

327.question: What is the maximum allowable number of Deputy Commissioners established under the CMTA?

choices.D: None

327.reason: Under Section 200 of CMTA, the maximum number of Deputy Commissioners is six (6).

328.question: Police Captain Peter de la Cruz was given a Deputation Order to visit and inspect. Is this a legitimate Deputation Order?

choices.A: Yes, because the authority shall be exercised outside of customs premises.
choices.B: No, because the exercise of power to visit and inspect is exclusive to customs officers.
choices.C: No, because the exercise of power to visit and inspect is subject to approval of the Secretary of Finance.
choices.D: Yes, because the power to visit and inspect is in the exercise of police authority under CMTA.

328.reason: The power to visit and inspect is exclusive to customs officers and cannot be delegated to police officers.

329.question: Who holds the authority to issue a Mission Order?

choices.A: The authority to issue a Mission Order.
choices.B: The Commissioner or his Deputy Commissioner of Customs.
choices.C: The authority is vested upon the Commissioner of Customs and any Deputy Commissioner of Customs and District Collectors.
choices.D: The authority is vested upon the Commissioner of Customs, Deputy Commissioner of Customs and District Collectors.

329.reason: The authority to issue a Mission Order is vested upon the Commissioner of Customs, Deputy Commissioners, and District Collectors.

330.question: Who carries the ultimate authority to open or close a port of entry?

choices.A: President of the Philippines upon the recommendation of the Commissioner of Customs.
choices.B: Secretary of Finance upon the recommendation of the Secretary of Finance.
choices.C: Secretary of Finance upon the recommendation of the Secretary of Finance.
choices.D: President of the Philippines upon the recommendation of the Secretary of Finance.

330.reason: The President of the Philippines has the ultimate authority to open or close a port of entry upon recommendation of the Commissioner of Customs.

331.question: If customs premises used for storage also serve as a dwelling, is a judicial search warrant required for police authority exercise under CMTA?

choices.A: Yes, because a family lives in the place.
choices.B: No, as specifically provided for under CMTA.
choices.C: No, unless the court decides to issue otherwise.
choices.D: No, unless it is indicated in the request for the issuance of warrant that the occupant is demanding for a search warrant.

331.reason: Under CMTA, customs officers may enter premises used as dwelling without a judicial warrant as specifically provided under the law.

332.question: Prior to R.A. 9280, the Supreme Court considered customs brokerage a business. Which case best reflects this legal viewpoint?

choices.A: Calvo v. UCPB General Insurance Co., Inc G.R. No. 149496, March 19, 2002 379 SCRA 510
choices.B: De Guzman v. Court of Appeals in relation to Article 1732 Civil Code of the Philippines.
choices.C: Kasparan ng mga Nagsisitinda sa Pamantasan ng Pilipinas v. Tan G.R. No. 81311, June 30 1988
choices.D: Remigio v. Sandiganbayan, January 18, 2002 374 SCRA 114

332.reason: Calvo v. UCPB General Insurance Co., Inc. considered customs brokerage as a business prior to R.A. 9280.

333.question: Which CMTA section provides for the legal obligation regarding the Duty of Officer to Disclose Official Character?

choices.A: Sec. 217
choices.B: Sec. 216
choices.C: Sec. 219
choices.D: Sec. 218

333.reason: Section 218 of the CMTA provides for the Duty of Officer to Disclose Official Character.

334.question: Currently, how many Collection Districts are established within the Bureau?
334.reason: There are currently sixteen (16) Collection Districts established within the Bureau of Customs.

335.question: Entry into customs premises requires prior authorization. Does this prohibition also extend to the adjoining streets or alleys of these facilities?

choices.A: No, as imported goods are not stored in these places.
choices.B: Yes, as explicitly provided for under CMTA.
choices.C: Yes, as imported goods may be stored in these places.
choices.D: None of the choices.

335.reason: The prohibition on entry without authorization also extends to adjoining streets and alleys as explicitly provided under CMTA.

336.question: Who is legally ineligible to exercise customs police authority under the CMTA?

choices.A: Customs Inspectors
choices.B: Customs Appraisers
choices.C: Warehouse Guards
choices.D: All of the above are authorized to perform police authority.

336.reason: Customs Inspectors, Customs Appraisers, and Warehouse Guards are all authorized to exercise police authority under the CMTA.

337.question: Is the proposition accurate that the Bureau of Customs's authority to collect customs duties is an absolute rule?

choices.A: Yes, because tax is the lifeblood of the economy.
choices.B: No, because such power is without prejudice to the general police power of the local government units, the PCG and law enforcement agencies in the exercise of their functions.
choices.C: Yes, because the control of customs jurisdiction does not admit any exception.
choices.D: Any of the above depending on the situation.

337.reason: The authority to collect customs duties is not absolute; it is without prejudice to the functions of other government agencies.

338.question: Under what conditions can a person exercising customs police authority legally force entry by opening gates?

choices.A: Presence of the owner of the imported goods.
choices.B: Presence of the owner of the place to be entered.
choices.C: Presence of either the District Collector who has territorial jurisdiction over the place or his authorized representative.
choices.D: Presence of Punong Barangay or his authorized representative and the police having jurisdiction over the area.

338.reason: The District Collector or his authorized representative must be present when forcing entry by opening gates.

339.question: Which official is granted the authority to declare any public wharf, landing place, infrastructure, street or land, in any port of entry under the jurisdiction of the Bureau of Customs as may be necessary, for customs purposes?

choices.A: District Collector who has territorial jurisdiction over the port.
choices.B: Commissioner of Customs.
choices.C: Commissioner of Customs subject to approval of the Secretary of Finance.
choices.D: President of the Philippines.

339.reason: The Commissioner of Customs may declare public infrastructure for customs purposes, subject to SOF approval.

340.question: If a customs official is questioned while exercising police powers, what is the legally required response from the authorized individual?

choices.A: The authorized person shall present his credentials and warrant of seizure.
choices.B: The authorized person shall disclose the source of information on why search is being conducted.
choices.C: The authorized person shall disclose the nature of the authority and exhibit the corresponding written authority issued by the Commissioner of Customs.
choices.D: Any of the above.

340.reason: The customs officer shall disclose the nature of the authority and exhibit the corresponding written authority issued by the Commissioner.

341.question: What are the grounds for the maintenance of an alert order?

choices.A: Prevention of unlawful importation, exportation of articles or goods.
choices.B: Intelligence report on smuggling activities of specific persons or firms.
choices.C: Intelligence report on smuggling activities as provided under CMTA.
choices.D: All of the above.

341.reason: Alert orders may be maintained on any of the stated grounds.

342.question: For how long is a Deputation Order considered legally valid?

choices.A: It shall be valid until suspended, cancelled or revoked by the issuing authority.
choices.B: Its validity shall not exceed one (1) year from issuance, unless earlier revoked for cause or when the purpose for which it was issued ceased to exist or when deputized officer is recalled by the head of agency.
choices.C: Its validity shall not exceed one (1) year from issuance.
choices.D: Its validity shall not exceed one (1) month from issuance and shall automatically be renewed if the purpose for which it was issued has continued to exist.

342.reason: A Deputation Order shall not exceed one (1) year from issuance, unless earlier revoked or recalled.

343.question: What is the extent of the validity period applicable to a Mission Order?

choices.A: It may only be exercised within the period prescribed in the Mission Order.
choices.B: It may be exercised within the period prescribed in the Mission Order and may be extended if warranted by similar circumstances.
choices.C: It may be exercised at any place or enclosure within the Philippines including free zones.
choices.D: It may be exercised in any place or enclosure within the Philippines including free zones.

343.reason: A Mission Order may only be exercised within the period prescribed in the order.

344.question: Who possesses the legal standing to file an application for a judicial warrant?

choices.A: The Commissioner and his Deputy Commissioner may apply for a judicial search warrant.
choices.B: Only officers in the Legal Service may apply for a judicial search warrant.
choices.C: Only the Commissioner and his Deputy Commissioner may apply for a judicial search warrant.
choices.D: Any of the choices.

344.reason: Only the Commissioner and his Deputy Commissioner may apply for a judicial search warrant under Section 222.

345.question: Who possesses the authority to officially issue a Deputation Order?

choices.A: Only the Commissioner of Customs may issue a Deputation Order.
choices.B: The Commissioner of Customs and any customs officer he authorizes in writing may issue a Deputation Order.
choices.C: Aside from the Commissioner of Customs, District Collectors within his territorial jurisdiction may issue a Deputation Order.
choices.D: The Commissioner of Customs has exclusive authority to issue a Deputation Order subject to approval of the Customs Personnel Order (CPO) by the Secretary of Finance.

345.reason: Only the Commissioner of Customs may issue a Deputation Order.

346.question: Under Section 7 of R.A. 11227, the Court of Tax Appeals exercises exclusive appellate jurisdiction over the decisions of the Commissioner. Which case underscores this specific principle?

choices.A: Emile v. Vinuya G.R. No. L-29043 37 SCRA 381
choices.B: Papa v. Mago G.R. No. L-27360 22, SCRA 857
choices.C: Asian Terminals Inc., v. Bautista Ricafort, 505 SCRA 748
choices.D: Senones v. Frias 89, SCRA 636

346.reason: Emile v. Vinuya established that the BOC has exclusive jurisdiction over forfeiture proceedings, with CTA having appellate jurisdiction.

347.question: Who bears the legal responsibility for ensuring the accuracy of the goods declaration but is not liable for the actual payment of duties and taxes?

choices.A: Carrying vessel
choices.B: Customs broker
choices.C: Declarant
choices.D: Bureau of Customs

347.reason: The customs broker is responsible for the accuracy of the goods declaration but not for the payment of duties and taxes.

348.question: Who authorizes the reassignment of customs officers?

choices.A: Commissioner of Customs
choices.B: District Collector subject to approval of the Commissioner of Customs.
choices.C: Commissioner of Customs subject to approval of the Secretary of Finance.
choices.D: Secretary of Finance subject to approval of the President of the Philippines.

348.reason: The Commissioner of Customs may reassign customs officers subject to the approval of the Secretary of Finance.

349.question: Is a separate Mission Order required to enforce a Letter of Authority?

choices.A: A LOA may be implemented without a need for a Mission Order.
choices.B: A Mission Order must be issued to authorize the implementation of a LOA.
choices.C: If LOA is exercised within customs premises there is no need for a MO.
choices.D: It depends on the Commissioner of Customs.

349.reason: A Mission Order must be issued to authorize the implementation of a Letter of Authority.

350.question: Which Collection District encompasses the jurisdiction over the sub-port of Mindanao Container Port?

choices.A: Cagayan De Oro
choices.B: Balangas
choices.C: Cebu
choices.D: Tacloban

350.reason: The sub-port of Mindanao Container Port is under Collection District No. X - Cagayan De Oro.

351.question: What is the appropriate course of action for customs officials if an inventory inspection reveals regulated/restricted goods without the necessary regulatory permits?

choices.A: The goods shall be seized.
choices.B: The visiting customs officers shall recommend to the Commissioner of Customs the issuance of WSD.
choices.C: The visiting customs officers are authorized to immediately condemn the goods.
choices.D: The visiting customs officers must immediately refer the matter to the concerned regulatory agency or agencies.

351.reason: When regulated/restricted goods are discovered without permits, the matter must be referred to the concerned regulatory agency.

352.question: Who has the authority to appoint the Commissioner and Deputy Commissioners of the Bureau of Customs?

choices.A: Secretary of Finance
choices.B: Congress
choices.C: President of the Philippines
choices.D: Court of Tax Appeals

352.reason: The President of the Philippines appoints the Commissioner and Deputy Commissioners of the Bureau of Customs.

353.question: What is the maximum number of Deputy Commissioners authorized under the CMTA to assist the Commissioner?

choices.A: Not less than 2
choices.B: Exactly 3
choices.C: At least 4 but not more than 6
choices.D: At least 5

353.reason: Under Section 200, the Commissioner shall be assisted by at least four (4) but not more than six (6) Deputy Commissioners.

354.question: Which CMTA section contains the legal provision regarding the 'Duty of Officer to Disclose Official Character'?

choices.A: Sec. 217
choices.B: Sec. 216
choices.C: Sec. 219
choices.D: Sec. 218

354.reason: Section 218 of the CMTA contains the Duty of Officer to Disclose Official Character.

355.question: Which specific legal case stands for the principle that the BOC has exclusive jurisdiction over seized and forfeited vehicles, preventing the RTC from intervening?

choices.A: Emile v. Vinuya G.R. No. L-29043 37 SCRA 381
choices.B: Papa v. Mago G.R. No. L-27360 22, SCRA 857
choices.C: Remigio v. Sandiganbayan, 374 SCRA 114
choices.D: Asian Terminals Inc., v. Bautista Ricafort, 505 SCRA 748

355.reason: Emile v. Vinuya stands for the principle that the BOC has exclusive jurisdiction over seizure and forfeiture of vehicles, preventing RTC intervention.

356.question: Within what duration must the Tariff Commission release its ruling on a tariff classification dispute, counting from the date it receives complete documents or after the hearing ends?

choices.A: The ruling must be promulgated within 30 working days.
choices.B: The ruling must be promulgated within 20 working days.
choices.C: The ruling must be promulgated within 15 working days.
choices.D: The ruling must be promulgated within 10 working days.

356.reason: The Tariff Commission must issue its ruling on tariff classification disputes within thirty (30) working days from receipt of complete documents or after the hearing.

357.question: What legal remedy is available to the importer if the Commissioner of Customs fails to render a decision within the statutory period on a protest case involving a valuation dispute?

choices.A: The importer may directly file an appeal with the Supreme Court.
choices.B: The importer may elevate the protest to the Secretary of Finance for automatic approval.
choices.C: The importer may file an appeal with the Court of Tax Appeals within 30 days from the lapse of the Commissioner's 30-day decision period.
choices.D: The importer may file a motion for reconsideration with the District Collector.

357.reason: If the Commissioner fails to act within 30 days, the importer may appeal to the Court of Tax Appeals within 30 days from the lapse of the Commissioner's decision period.

358.question: For a regulated goods importation, if the required import permit is obtained only after the goods have already arrived, when must the importer submit this permit to the Bureau of Customs?

choices.A: Upon payment of the duties and taxes.
choices.B: Upon lodgement of the goods declaration.
choices.C: At any time prior to the release of the goods from customs control.
choices.D: During the Post Clearance Audit phase.

358.reason: The import permit must be submitted at any time prior to the release of the goods from customs custody.

359.question: If an importer declares 'payment under protest' to the Commissioner of Customs two months after the cargo has already been released, what is the legal treatment of this filing?

choices.A: The Commissioner is deemed to have automatically denied the protest due to inaction.
choices.B: The Commissioner must rule on the protest within 30 days of receipt.
choices.C: The protest is deemed denied outright for being filed beyond the allowable appeal period.
choices.D: The protest will be endorsed to the Secretary of Finance for final disposition.

359.reason: Protests must be filed within the prescribed period. Filing two months after release is beyond the allowable appeal period, thus the protest is denied outright.

360.question: Under CMTA rules, how many copies of the goods declaration are generally required to be filed with the Bureau?

choices.A: It shall be filed in a single copy only.
choices.B: It shall be filed in duplicate.
choices.C: It shall be filed in triplicate.
choices.D: The number of copies shall be strictly based on the importer's preference.

360.reason: Under the CMTA electronic system, the goods declaration is generally filed in a single electronic copy.

361.question: If a customs broker files the goods declaration on behalf of his client, what specific document/s must be submitted together with the declaration to validate the transaction?

choices.A: The notarized contract of the broker.
choices.B: The official receipt for the brokerage fee.
choices.C: The valid professional license of the customs broker.
choices.D: The written authorization from the client.

361.reason: The customs broker must submit written authorization from the client to validate the transaction.

362.question: Which agency is tasked with issuing the Certificate of Tax Exemption for the importation of machinery and equipment under the BOI rules?

choices.A: Board of Investments (BOI)
choices.B: Bureau of Customs
choices.C: Department of Finance
choices.D: Department of Trade and Industry

362.reason: The Board of Investments (BOI) issues the Certificate of Tax Exemption for BOI-registered importations.

363.question: What should be the timeframe for the District Collector to issue the formal 'Notice to Mark Imported Goods' to the importer?

choices.A: Within 5 days from the physical examination of the imported goods.
choices.B: Within 5 days from the payment of the 5% marking duty.
choices.C: Within 5 days from the lodgement of the goods declaration.
choices.D: Within 5 days from the discharge of the goods from the carrying vessel.

363.reason: The Notice to Mark Imported Goods shall be issued within 5 days from the lodgement of the goods declaration.

364.question: If the importer or declarant fails to lodge the goods declaration within the initial 15-day period, but files it 20 days later, and the duties and taxes have been fully settled, does the importer retain the right to reclaim the goods?

choices.A: No, the goods are automatically deemed abandoned.
choices.B: Yes, but only if a penal surcharge is paid.
choices.C: Yes, the importer may still reclaim the goods.
choices.D: No, the goods are immediately forfeited in favor of the government.

364.reason: Even if filed beyond the 15-day period, the importer may still reclaim the goods upon payment of duties and taxes and applicable penalties.

365.question: When assessing the validity of a search warrant used by customs authorities, what is the required form and minimum content of this warrant?

choices.A: Must be in writing and must particularly describe the place to be searched and the things to be seized.
choices.B: Must be in writing and approved by the Secretary of Finance.
choices.C: Must be in writing and must state the probable cause.
choices.D: Must be in writing and must name the specific customs officer.

365.reason: A valid search warrant must be in writing and particularly describe the place to be searched and the things to be seized.

366.question: During a search of a vessel or aircraft for customs violations, when is such an inspection legally permitted to be conducted?

choices.A: Only during daytime hours.
choices.B: Only during regular office hours.
choices.C: At any time of the day or night.
choices.D: Only after obtaining judicial clearance.

366.reason: Under CMTA, customs authorities may search vessels or aircraft at any time of the day or night.

367.question: If a valuation dispute is raised before the District Collector, and it is determined that the matter lacks highly technical difficulty regarding customs valuation, what is the recourse of the importer regarding the release of their shipment?

choices.A: The shipment can be released under tentative assessment, subject to the District Collector's approval.
choices.B: The importer must wait for the decision of the Commissioner of Customs first.
choices.C: The shipment cannot be released until the valuation is fully settled.
choices.D: The importer may release the shipment by absolute right without any need for approval.

367.reason: For simple valuation disputes, the shipment may be released under tentative assessment upon posting of sufficient security.

368.question: What is the legal consequence for the bonded goods stored in a Customs Bonded Warehouse (CBW) if the importer/operator fails to withdraw them within the prescribed storage period?

choices.A: The goods shall be immediately forfeited in favor of the government.
choices.B: The goods shall be subject to a monthly 5% storage surcharge.
choices.C: The goods shall be deemed expressly abandoned.
choices.D: The goods shall be sold at a public auction and the proceeds shall go to the importer.

368.reason: Goods stored in a CBW that are not withdrawn within the prescribed period shall be deemed expressly abandoned.

369.question: When the Bureau of Customs finds a simple classification issue that does not require highly technical evaluation, and it endorses the matter to the Tariff Commission, what is the appropriate action of the Commission?

choices.A: The Commission is obliged to conduct a full hearing.
choices.B: The Commission may decline the case if it finds no complex issue.
choices.C: The Commission must immediately endorse the matter to the Court of Tax Appeals.
choices.D: The Commission must automatically issue a ruling based on the BOC's findings.

369.reason: The Tariff Commission may decline simple classification cases that do not involve complex technical issues.

370.question: If an assessment dispute involves a combination of tariff classification and valuation issues, and resolving the classification is necessary to resolve the valuation, how should this be handled?

choices.A: The Tariff Commission shall handle the classification dispute, and the District Collector will handle the valuation dispute separately.
choices.B: The District Collector shall resolve the entire case simultaneously.
choices.C: The District Collector should refer the matter to the Tariff Commission and await the classification ruling before proceeding with the valuation.
choices.D: The case shall be elevated directly to the Court of Tax Appeals for a consolidated ruling.

370.reason: When classification is indispensable to valuation, the District Collector must await the Tariff Commission's ruling on classification before resolving valuation.

371.question: If an importer files an appeal from a Decision of the Tariff Commission (TC) denying a Motion for Reconsideration, what is the prescribed timeline for filing the appeal with the Secretary of Finance?

choices.A: Within 15 days from receipt of the denial.
choices.B: Within 30 days from receipt of the denial.
choices.C: Within 10 days from receipt of the denial.
choices.D: Within 7 days from receipt of the denial.

371.reason: Appeal to the Secretary of Finance from a TC decision denying an MR must be filed within thirty (30) days from receipt of the denial.

372.question: For the importation of prohibited or infringing goods where the declarant is unaware of the true nature of the goods, what is the penalty prescribed by the CMTA?

choices.A: The goods are deemed automatically forfeited, but no fine is imposed.
choices.B: The importer must pay a fine equal to 100% of the value of the goods.
choices.C: The goods are seized, and the declarant is subject to criminal prosecution.
choices.D: The goods are forfeited, and the importer pays an administrative fine.

372.reason: Even if the declarant is unaware, the goods are forfeited and an administrative fine is imposed under the CMTA.

373.question: Under the CMTA, when is the goods declaration considered to be 'lodged' for customs purposes?

choices.A: At the time the declaration is received by the customs official.
choices.B: At the time the declaration is electronically submitted to the Bureau of Customs.
choices.C: At the time the supporting documents are physically submitted to the Customs office.
choices.D: At the time the payment for duties and taxes is made.

373.reason: The goods declaration is considered lodged upon its electronic submission to the Bureau of Customs.

374.question: An importer receives a Final Assessment Notice (FAN) dated April 1 and fully pays the assessed amount on April 17. What is the legal status of the imported goods?

choices.A: The goods are deemed lawfully released from customs custody.
choices.B: The goods are deemed impliedly abandoned.
choices.C: The goods are deemed legally forfeited without option for recovery.
choices.D: The goods are deemed automatically seized.

374.reason: Upon full payment of the assessed duties and taxes, the goods are deemed lawfully released from customs custody.

375.question: When customs authorities conduct a search, what specific body or official is legally authorized to issue the corresponding search warrant?

choices.A: The Commissioner of Customs.
choices.B: The Collector of Customs.
choices.C: A Judge of the Regional Trial Court.
choices.D: The Secretary of Justice.

375.reason: Only a Judge of the Regional Trial Court is authorized to issue a search warrant.

376.question: When it comes to marking imported goods, can the marking be performed outside of customs premises?

choices.A: Yes, it may be done at the consignee's warehouse upon the importer's request and approval.
choices.B: No, marking is strictly required to be done while the goods are still within customs custody.
choices.C: Yes, it may be done anywhere as long as a customs representative is present.
choices.D: No, unless the goods are perishable.

376.reason: Marking of imported goods is strictly required to be done while the goods are still within customs custody.

377.question: What represents the best evidence to prove that imported goods are exempt from the payment of duties and taxes?

choices.A: The commercial invoice showing the value of the goods.
choices.B: The bill of lading and packing list.
choices.C: The valid tax exemption certificate or permit issued by the concerned government agency.
choices.D: The sworn statement of the importer.

377.reason: The best evidence of tax exemption is the valid tax exemption certificate or permit issued by the concerned government agency.

378.question: When the Tariff Commission is hearing a tariff classification dispute, are they mandated to conduct a formal hearing?

choices.A: Yes, a full-blown hearing is mandatory for all disputes.
choices.B: No, the Commission is not mandated to conduct a hearing unless it deems necessary for fact-finding.
choices.C: Yes, but only if the importer specifically requests it.
choices.D: No, the BOC is strictly required to handle the entire hearing process.

378.reason: The Tariff Commission is not mandated to conduct a hearing unless it deems necessary for fact-finding.

379.question: An importer requests the advance ruling on ROO for a transaction. If the Tariff Commission modifies the ruling and the importer fails to file an MR or appeal, when does the ruling become final and executory?

choices.A: Immediately upon receipt of the modified ruling.
choices.B: After the lapse of the 15-day period for filing an MR.
choices.C: After the lapse of the 30-day period for filing an appeal to the Secretary of Finance.
choices.D: It never becomes final and executory without an MR.

379.reason: If no MR or appeal is filed, the ruling becomes final and executory after the lapse of the 30-day appeal period to the Secretary of Finance.

380.question: In what specific circumstances is an importer allowed to file an amended goods declaration?

choices.A: Only before the goods are examined by customs.
choices.B: Only after the Notice of Assessment has been issued.
choices.C: Only when the assessment is based on a post-clearance audit.
choices.D: Only when the Bureau of Customs makes an assessment mistake.

381.question: Who among the following entities is considered the 'ultimate purchaser' for the purposes of complying with the customs marking requirement?

383.question: In the absence of a specific Deputy District Collector, who is legally authorized to temporarily perform the duties of the District Collector?

choices.D: Within 7 working days.

385.question: When the evidence of payment for duties and taxes is presented during the forfeiture proceedings, what is the immediate duty of the District Collector?

387.question: For goods that are subject to an advance ruling request, if the importer files the goods declaration 60 days after the ruling is requested but before the ruling is issued, what happens to the pending advance ruling application?

388.question: An importer protested a valuation assessment within the prescribed timeframe. The Commissioner fails to act on the protest within the 30-day period. How can the importer seek relief?

389.question: Who has the legal power to designate or issue a Deputation Order authorizing a person to exercise police authority?

392.question: If a customs officer performs a search without a valid search warrant, and no legal exception exists, what is the officer exposed to?

396.question: What are the conditions that disqualify an importer from being allowed to release their goods under Tentative Assessment?

396.reason: Tentative assessment is not allowed for disputes involving complex classification or highly technical ROO issues.

397.question: When are goods deemed 'entered' for consumption under the CMTA electronic lodgement system?

398.question: If the Tariff Commission denies an importer's motion for reconsideration based on newly discovered evidence, how many MRs is the importer allowed to file?
